topicName: The Founding of Rome & Early Kings

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Founding of Rome & Early Kings
cards.back: Roman legend traced Rome's origins to Aeneas (Trojan refugee) and the founding by Romulus and Remus (753 BC)

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Founding of Rome & Early Kings
cards.back: The seven kings ruled Rome from its founding until the overthrow of Tarquin the Proud (Superbus) in 509 BC

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Founding of Rome & Early Kings
cards.back: The last king, Tarquin Superbus, was a tyrant whose son Sextus raped Lucretia, triggering the rebellion led by Brutus

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Founding of Rome & Early Kings
cards.back: The Republic (res publica = 'public thing') replaced the monarchy: power was held by elected magistrates and the Senate

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Founding of Rome & Early Kings
cards.back: Roman society was divided between Patricians (aristocratic families) and Plebeians (common citizens); the plebeians struggled for political rights

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Founding of Rome & Early Kings
cards.back: The early Republic established key offices: two consuls (chief magistrates with one-year terms), the Senate (advisory council of patricians)
